text: If you ask me, I think that for a man there is no misery unless there be something in the universe which he thinks miserable.
plain: Things only wreck you if you decide they do.

text: A long life includes all these troubles, just as a long journey includes dust and mud and rain.
plain: You asked for a long life, so you asked for the hard parts too.

text: The road to vice is not only downhill, but steep; and many men are rendered incorrigible by the fact that, while in all other crafts errors bring shame to good craftsmen and cause vexation to those who go astray, the errors of life are a positive source of pleasure.
plain: Bad habits feel good while you do them, which is why they are so hard to quit.

text: A good conscience, however, wishes to come forth and be seen of men; wickedness fears the very shadows.
plain: If you are proud of what you do, you have nothing to hide.

text: Good luck frees many men from punishment, but no man from fear.
plain: You can get away with it and still never relax.

text: You need never believe that anyone who depends upon happiness is happy!
plain: If your joy depends on things outside you, it is not really yours.

text: It is tragic for the soul to be apprehensive of the future and wretched in anticipation of wretchedness, consumed with an anxious desire that the objects which give pleasure may remain in its possession to the very end.
plain: Dreading the loss of what you have wrecks the enjoyment of having it.

text: And there is no difference between grief for something lost and the fear of losing it.
plain: Fearing a loss already hurts like the loss.

text: And there is nothing more wretched or foolish than premature fear. What madness it is to anticipate one’s troubles!
plain: Stop suffering in advance for things that may never happen.

text: He who can bear Fortune, can also beware of Fortune.
plain: If you can take a hit, you are better at dodging one.

text: To have may be taken from us, to have had, never.
plain: What you had and enjoyed cannot be undone.

text: We must lose our lives as surely as we lose our property, and this, if we understand the truth, is itself a consolation. Lose it with equanimity; for you must lose your life also.
plain: You will lose everything anyway, so lose things calmly.

text: Chance robs us of the thing, but leaves us its use and its enjoyment—and we have lost this if we are so unfair as to regret.
plain: Luck takes the thing but not the good you got from it, unless you waste that on regret.

text: Pain he endures, death he awaits.
plain: Take pain head on and meet death calmly.

text: The past is ours, and there is nothing more secure for us than that which has been.
plain: Nobody can take back what already happened to you.

text: Periods of time separate us, but death levels us.
plain: Age and rank separate us for now, death makes us equal.

text: Whoever complains about the death of anyone, is complaining that he was a man.
plain: Griefing that people die is arguing with being human.

text: Life is neither a Good nor an Evil; it is simply the place where good and evil exist.
plain: Life is the arena, not the verdict. What you do in it decides.

text: Yours is not pain; it is a mere sting—and it is you yourself who are turning it into pain.
plain: A lot of what you call suffering is you inflating a small hit.

text: And yet all men complain about the one thing wherein none of them is deceived.
plain: Death is the one promise life keeps, and we still complain.

text: The display of grief makes more demands than grief itself: how few men are sad in their own company!
plain: Much of our show of pain is for the audience.

text: Everything is slippery, treacherous, and more shifting than any weather.
plain: Nothing stays put, so do not build on it staying the same.

text: O what madness it is to plot out far-reaching hopes!
plain: Do not stake your whole life on a future you do not own.

text: No one has any right to draw for himself upon the future.
plain: Tomorrow is not yours to spend yet.

text: Time does indeed roll along by fixed law, but as in darkness; and what is it to me whether Nature’s course is sure, when my own is unsure?
plain: Time keeps its schedule, but you do not know yours.

text: Let us postpone nothing. Let us balance life’s account every day.
plain: Close out each day as if it could be the last.

text: The greatest flaw in life is that it is always imperfect, and that a certain part of it is postponed.
plain: The thing that ruins a life is putting parts of it off.

text: We must get rid of this craving for life, and learn that it makes no difference when your suffering comes, because at some time you are bound to suffer.
plain: Suffering is coming either way, so stop bargaining for more time.

text: The point is, not how long you live, but how nobly you live.
plain: Length of life matters less than how you live it.

text: That day, which you fear as being the end of all things, is the birthday of your eternity.
plain: The day you dread may be a beginning.

text: Survey everything that lies about you, as if it were luggage in a guest-chamber: you must travel on.
plain: You are a guest here. Hold your stuff loosely.

text: Nature strips you as bare at your departure as at your entrance.
plain: You leave with nothing, same as you came.

text: Nothing has corrupted oratory and all other studies that depend on hearing so much as popular approval.
plain: Chasing applause ruins the work.

text: Why are you looking about for troubles which may perhaps come your way, but which may indeed not come your way at all?
plain: You are scanning for disasters that probably will not arrive.

text: A man may be wise without parade and without arousing enmity.
plain: Be good at what you do quietly.

text: That from which you are running, is within you.
plain: What you are running from travels with you.

text: Your ambition will be so frenzied that you will regard yourself last in the race if there is anyone in front of you.
plain: Comparison makes you feel poor and behind no matter how far you have come.

text: If you are wise, mingle these two elements: do not hope without despair, or despair without hope.
plain: Expect the worst while hoping for the best, and never fully either one.

text: Others are snatched from sight; we ourselves are being stealthily filched away from ourselves.
plain: You are changing and losing time every day too, you just do not see it.

text: Regard everything that pleases you as if it were a flourishing plant; make the most of it while it is in leaf, for different plants at different seasons must fall and die.
plain: Enjoy what you have while it is green.

text: It is medicine, not scenery, for which the sick man must go a-searching.
plain: A change of scenery will not heal what is wrong with you.

text: The only harbour safe from the seething storms of this life is scorn of the future, a firm stand, a readiness to receive Fortune’s missiles full in the breast, neither skulking nor turning the back.
plain: Safety is stopping fearing what comes and standing your ground.

text: Many a sight that is held a terror in the night-time, is turned to ridicule by day.
plain: Fears shrink once you look at them in daylight.

text: Our lack of confidence is not the result of difficulty; the difficulty comes from our lack of confidence.
plain: It is not hard, you just doubt yourself.

text: If you set a high value on liberty, you must set a low value on everything else.
plain: Freedom costs you the need for stuff.

text: Nothing, however, will help you so much as keeping still—talking very little with others, and as much as may be with yourself.
plain: Talk less, and spend time with your own thoughts.

text: You will escape envy if you do not force yourself upon the public view, if you do not boast your possessions, if you understand how to enjoy things privately.
plain: Do not flaunt it and people will leave you alone.

text: The most important contribution to peace of mind is never to do wrong.
plain: A clean conscience is the first step to calm.

text: Whoever expects punishment, receives it, but whoever deserves it, expects it.
plain: If you did wrong, you will spend your days waiting for the hit.

text: No man is at the mercy of affairs. He gets entangled in them of his own accord, and then flatters himself that being busy is a proof of happiness.
plain: Being busy is a choice, and it is not the same as being happy.

text: Just as we suffer from excess in all things, so we suffer from excess in literature; thus we learn our lessons, not for life, but for the lecture-room.
plain: Do not study to sound smart. Learn to live.

text: Life is not a dainty business.
plain: Life is rough, so expect that.

text: Everyone approaches courageously a danger which he has prepared himself to meet long before, and withstands even hardships if he has previously practised how to meet them.
plain: Rehearse the hard thing ahead of time and it loses its power.

text: Whatever happens, assume that it was bound to happen, and do not be willing to rail at Nature.
plain: It was always going to happen, so stop fighting reality.

text: Let us live thus, and speak thus; let Fate find us ready and alert.
plain: Be ready when it hits.

text: You have started on a long journey; you are bound to slip, collide, fall, become weary, and cry out: “O for Death!”—or in other words, tell lies.
plain: You will fall and want to quit. Expect it and do not mean it.

text: Absorb not all that you wish, but all that you can hold.
plain: Take on only what you can carry.

text: Let every day, as soon as it comes, be welcome as being the choicest, and let it be made our own possession. We must catch that which flees.
plain: Grab each day, because it is leaving.

text: We should so learn them that words may become deeds.
plain: Only learning that turns into action counts.

text: One must steer, not talk.
plain: Do the work, do not talk about it.

text: I shall show you how men can prove their words to be their own: it is by doing what they have been talking about.
plain: Your words are yours only when you act on them.

text: The poor lack much; the greedy man lacks all.
plain: Greed leaves you with nothing, no matter how much you have.

text: None of us has sifted out the truth; we have passed fear on to one another; none has dared to approach the object which caused his dread, and to understand the nature of his fear—aye, the good behind it.
plain: Most fear is inherited and never examined.

text: What is necessary will meet you everywhere; what is superfluous has always to be hunted out—and with great endeavour.
plain: What you need is easy to find. Wants take a long chase.

text: The time to admire your own conduct is when you have come to despise the necessities.
plain: Giving up luxuries is easy. Mastery is not needing the basics.

text: Why wonder? Why gape in astonishment? It is all show; such things are displayed, not possessed; while they please they pass away.
plain: Flashy wealth is for show and it fades.

text: I came to despise riches, not because of their uselessness, but because of their pettiness.
plain: Wealth is not evil, it is small.

text: If you are willing to think often of these things, you will strive not to seem happy, but to be happy, and, in addition, to seem happy to yourself rather than to others.
plain: Be happy for real, not for show.

text: Men love and hate their vices at the same time.
plain: You can hate a habit and still want it.

text: Self-Command is the greatest command of all.
plain: Ruling yourself is the biggest power there is.

text: Those who wish their virtue to be advertised are not striving for virtue but for renown.
plain: Doing good for applause is chasing fame, not goodness.

text: You need not look about for the reward of a just deed; a just deed in itself offers a still greater return.
plain: Doing right is its own payment.

text: There are never any occasions when you need think yourself safe because you wield the weapons of Fortune; fight with your own!
plain: Do not rely on luck or borrowed advantages. Build your own.

text: And what is Bravery? It is the impregnable fortress for our mortal weakness; when a man has surrounded himself therewith, he can hold out free from anxiety during life’s siege; for he is using his own strength and his own weapons.
plain: Courage is the fort that protects you from everything else.
